documents.title: Work Exam
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The plant is sending everyone on the machines through an annual exam at their occupational health clinic this month. Do you need to fill anything out or do I just go?

documents.title: Re: Work Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Nothing needed from us. Go ahead, and sign their release so the results come here too. We'll still see you for your own physical this summer.

documents.title: Occupational Health Examination
documents.author: occupational medicine
documents.body:
Occupational Health Services
Date of service: 06/23/2025
Reason: annual employer-required examination, machine operator

History: Has run the folding and gluing equipment at the plant for close to eight years. Asks for the overnight shift whenever it is open; says the plant is quieter with fewer people around. Per his supervisor's input on the employer form, he is on time, efficient, never involved in conflict, and talks with coworkers only as much as the job requires.

Outside work his interests are all solitary: he makes sculptures out of scrap cardboard from the line and reads equipment and technical manuals. He spends evenings at his computer keeping spreadsheets and files that track things like his household electricity use and daily step counts. No close friends. Little contact with family apart from a birthday email to his mother. Has never dated and says he does not see why he would. He is content with all of this and calls it a comfortable, efficient way to live.

Denies low mood, hopelessness, or change in sleep or appetite. No history of hallucinations, delusions, disorganized thinking, or manic or hypomanic periods. Describes himself as a quiet child who chose the library over playground games; teachers saw him as bright but hard to draw out. Denies trauma, bullying or abuse. No alcohol, tobacco or drug use.

Current medications: none. Allergies: NKDA. Known diagnoses: schizoid personality disorder (per primary care, 2024). Family history noncontributory.

Exam: Alert and oriented, groomed appropriately. Speech sparse but coherent. Affect flat; mood "fine." Thought process linear, content unremarkable. Limited insight into his social withdrawal, which he does not regard as a problem. General physical examination normal; vision and hearing screens passed.

Labs: CBC, metabolic panel and thyroid function within normal limits.

Determination: Meets requirements; medically cleared to continue in current position.

Comment to primary care: Given a lifelong pattern of detachment and limited emotional expression, a psychiatric evaluation could be considered at your discretion.

Occupational medicine physician

documents.title: Outside Letter Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Occupational health letter reviewed. Cleared for work, labs normal there so no need to repeat at his physical. Their picture matches what he told me last year. They suggest psychiatry; will raise it at his physical next week.

documents.title: Missed Physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient called back after our portal note about the missed 2:30. Covered an extra overnight shift and slept through his alarm. Apologetic. Rebooked to Tues 7/22 at 2:30.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33 y/o M, annual exam. Feels well. Still on nights at the plant and doing writing work during the day.

Went over the occupational health letter with him. He agrees with how they described him and is unbothered by it. Offered a psychiatry evaluation as they suggested, framed as a chance to have a specialist confirm the picture and talk through options. He declined: does not feel anything needs fixing. Respected; told him the offer stands.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
ROS: negative. Sleep regular on his schedule. Appetite normal.

Exam: Vitals normal, weight steady. Calm, brief, cooperative. Affect restricted, consistent with prior. Heart, lungs, abdomen, skin normal.

PHQ-9: 1.

A/P:
1. Schizoid personality disorder: stable, no distress, declines referral for now.
2. Health maintenance: labs done by occupational health in June, normal; none today. Flu shot in the fall. Tdap good until 2027.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: No fever, no prior vaccine reaction. 2025-26 trivalent flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Observed 15 min, fine. Declined COVID shot here this year.

orders.reason: Evaluation of schizoid personality disorder at patient request

documents.title: That Psychiatry Thing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Last summer you offered a referral to a psychiatrist. My sister has been on me about it since the holidays. Her view is that I never connect with anyone. I don't agree there is a problem but I'd rather go once than keep having the conversation. Can you set it up? Afternoons only.

documents.title: Re: That Psychiatry Thing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Happy to. Referral sent to outpatient psychiatry with a note that you work nights and need an afternoon slot. Their office will contact you through the number on file, so you may want to leave your ringer on in the afternoons for a week or two. One visit commits you to nothing.

documents.title: Psychiatry Appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Psychiatry office called: couldn't reach patient by phone, so they mailed a letter and asked us to pass along that he is booked for an intake June 9 at 3:00 pm. Portal message sent to patient with the date.

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry
Initial evaluation, date of service 06/09/2026
Referred by primary care

Thank you for sending Mr. Finn. He came at the urging of his sister, who worries that he does not connect with anyone. He came to settle the question rather than with any concern of his own.

Background: Your 2024 exam recorded his preference for solitude and a diagnosis of schizoid personality disorder; his 2025 occupational health exam described the same pattern. No prior psychiatric treatment.

History: He writes technical documentation freelance from home and continues on the overnight shift at the box plant. Has lived in the same one-room apartment for eight years. His free time goes to reading up on little-known historical subjects, single-player computer games, and long walks by himself late at night. He has never had a romantic partner and cannot remember when he last saw a friend face to face. Finds family get-togethers tiring and tends to leave early after talking with very few people.

Review of symptoms: No sadness, anhedonia, sleep or appetite change, or suicidal ideation. No suspiciousness, magical thinking or perceptual disturbance. He is satisfied with how he lives and says he does best when people leave him alone.

Substances: never smoked, no alcohol. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA. Family psychiatric history: noncontributory.

Mental status: Flat affect. Answers brief, little spontaneous speech. Thought process linear and goal directed. No hallucinations or delusions.

Assessment: Presentation is consistent with schizoid personality disorder. No mood, anxiety or psychotic disorder identified.

Plan:
- No medication is indicated.
- Individual psychotherapy was offered; he declined, as he does not experience his situation as a problem.
- Follow-up with psychiatry as needed; he knows he can call to return.
- Ongoing care with primary care.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Psychiatry Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got the psychiatrist's letter. They agree with the diagnosis, don't recommend any medication, and left the door open if you ever want therapy. Nothing changes on our end. We can talk more at your physical in July if you like.

documents.title: Re: Psychiatry Visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: That matches what I expected. I forwarded the summary to my sister. See you in July.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34 y/o M, yearly exam. No concerns.

Interval: saw outpatient psychiatry in June. Letter reviewed: diagnosis confirmed, no medication, declined therapy, follow up as needed. He says the visit was fine and his sister has eased off. Same two jobs, same routine.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.
ROS: negative.

Exam: Vitals normal, weight unchanged. Brief, polite, restricted affect as before. No psychotic features. HEENT, neck, heart, lungs, abdomen, skin, extremities normal.

PHQ-9: 2.

A/P:
1. Schizoid personality disorder: stable. Psychiatry available if he changes his mind.
2. Health maintenance: up to date. No labs needed this year. Flu shot booked for late September. Tdap due next year.
RTC 1 year, portal in between.
